front: How is recession dating formally defined in classical business cycle analysis?
back: The identification of an alternating partition of discrete time into expansions terminating at cyclical peaks and contractions terminating at cyclical troughs, satisfying strict phase alternation and duration censoring constraints.

front: What are the Three D's evaluated by the NBER Business Cycle Dating Committee?
back: Depth (severity of output, employment, and income decline), Diffusion (breadth across independent industries and sectors), and Duration (persistence over time).

front: What minimum duration constraints are enforced by the standard Bry-Boschan (1971) cycle dating algorithm?
back: A minimum phase duration of 6 months (peak-to-trough or trough-to-peak) and a minimum cycle duration of 15 months (peak-to-peak or trough-to-trough).

front: Why does evaluating a trading strategy on unlagged historical NBER recession dates introduce look-ahead bias?
back: The NBER committee announces turning points retrospectively with delays of 4 to 21 months, so unlagged backtests utilize future committee determinations unavailable at historical trade dates.

front: Common Misconception: Is an economic recession legally defined as two consecutive quarters of negative real GDP growth?
back: No. The NBER explicitly rejects mechanical GDP rules, evaluating monthly coincident labor, income, sales, and output data; in 2001, a recession occurred without two consecutive negative GDP quarters.

front: What is the yield-curve recession signal, and what constitutes an inversion?
back: The term spread between long-term and short-term benchmark government bond yields (typically 10Y minus 3M). An inversion occurs when the spread is negative (short rates exceed long rates).

front: What is the mathematical specification of a binary probit recession-probability model?
back: Pr(R_{t+k} = 1 | S_t) = Phi(alpha + beta * S_t), where Phi is the standard normal cumulative distribution function and S_t is the term spread.

front: Why does the binary probit log-likelihood function possess a unique global maximum?
back: Because its Hessian matrix is strictly negative definite everywhere, proving that the sample log-likelihood is strictly concave over all parameter space.

front: What is the Estrella & Mishkin (1998) pseudo-R2 formula for probit models?
back: R2_EM = 1 - (ln(L_u) / ln(L_c))^(-(2/T) * ln(L_c)), where ln(L_u) is the unconstrained log-likelihood and ln(L_c) is the intercept-only constrained log-likelihood.

front: At what forecasting horizon does the yield-curve term spread achieve its peak pseudo-R2 in Estrella & Mishkin (1998)?
back: At the 4-quarter (12-month) forward horizon, achieving a pseudo-R2 of approximately 0.29 to 0.30 and outperforming stock returns and leading macro indices.

front: What is the critical term spread formula for a 50% predicted recession probability in a probit model?
back: S* = -alpha / beta, the spread where the linear latent index z = alpha + beta * S* equals zero so Phi(0) = 0.50.

front: Common Misconception: Does an un-inversion (steepening back to positive) mean the recession threat has passed?
back: No. Recessions historically begin after the curve has begun steepening ('bull steepening'), because central banks slash short-term policy rates as downturns materialize.

front: What are stock-bond correlation regimes?
back: Persistent multi-year macroeconomic regimes characterized by the sign of stock-bond return correlation: positive under supply-shock regimes (inflation bets) and negative under demand-shock regimes (deflation hedges).

front: What were the empirical average stock-bond return correlations in the US before and after 1998?
back: Positive correlation (~+0.35) from 1965 through 1997, flipping to negative correlation (~-0.40) from 1998 through 2021.

front: What macroeconomic condition governs the sign of the stock-bond return covariance under Campbell, Pflueger & Viceira (2020)?
back: The covariance between real output growth and inflation: supply shocks induce negative growth-inflation covariance, driving Cov(r_S, r_B) > 0, while demand shocks induce positive growth-inflation covariance, driving Cov(r_S, r_B) < 0.

front: How much annual volatility reduction does a negative stock-bond correlation (-0.40) provide to a 60/40 portfolio?
back: Approximately 2.0 to 3.5 percentage points of annualized portfolio volatility compared to an equivalent positive correlation (+0.40) regime.

front: Why did Risk Parity funds suffer massive drawdowns during calendar year 2022?
back: Because surging supply-side inflation caused stock-bond correlations to flip sharply positive (+0.55), inflicting simultaneous double-digit drawdowns on equities and leveraged nominal Treasuries.

front: Common Misconception: Are nominal sovereign bonds a universal hedge against equity market downturns?
back: No. Nominal bonds hedge equities only during demand-shock recessions; during supply shocks and inflation surges, bond yields spike as equities decline, destroying hedging efficacy.

front: How are macroeconomic inflation regimes defined in quantitative asset allocation?
back: Discrete price environments separating low/stable inflation (CPI in 1-3%) from inflation surges (CPI > 4% or accelerating), altering real asset returns and valuation multiples.

front: What is the average historical real return of US equities and nominal bonds during inflationary surges in Neville et al. (2021)?
back: US equities averaged -7% annualized real return and 10-year US Treasuries averaged -5% annualized real return across all major historical inflationary surges.

front: Which asset classes deliver the highest positive real returns during inflationary surges according to Neville et al. (2021)?
back: Commodities (+14% overall, +41% in energy) and Trend-Following / CTA momentum (+25% annualized real return).

front: Why does the real return loss of a nominal bond scale super-linearly with duration during an unexpected inflation shock?
back: Because nominal bonds suffer a double penalty: duration-driven capital loss (-n * theta * delta_pi) compounded by direct purchasing power dilution (-delta_pi), yielding total real return -(n * theta + 1) * delta_pi.

front: What is the contango roll yield drag in commodity futures investing?
back: The negative return incurred when rolling expiring commodity futures into higher-priced forward contracts (R_roll = (S - F) / F < 0), which can erase capital during non-inflationary periods.

front: Common Misconception: Are equities a reliable hedge against unexpected inflation surges?
back: No. Despite owning real assets, equities suffer valuation multiple compression from higher discount rates and corporate margin contraction, losing real purchasing power during surges.

front: What is real-time regime classification in quantitative macroeconomics?
back: The causal sequential estimation of discrete state probabilities xi_{t|t} = Pr(S_t = j | I_t) conditioned strictly on point-in-time information without future data leakage.

front: What is the Hamilton (1989) forward filter Bayesian updating recursion for filtered state probabilities?
back: xi_{t|t} = (xi_{t|t-1} (*) eta_t) / (1' (xi_{t|t-1} (*) eta_t)), where xi_{t|t-1} = P' * xi_{t-1|t-1} and eta_t is the measurement density vector.

front: Why is the Hamilton posterior filter information monotonic?
back: Because the posterior odds ratio Omega_{j/i, t|t} equals prior odds multiplied by the observation likelihood ratio eta_{j, t} / eta_{i, t}, depending strictly on causal point-in-time data.

front: What is the difference between filtered probabilities xi_{t|t} and Kim smoothed probabilities xi_{t|T}?
back: Filtered probabilities use only observations up to t (causal), while smoothed probabilities use the full sample up to T, incorporating future data to resolve historical states retroactively.

front: How do continuous quadrant probabilities prevent destructive turnover in regime-switching portfolios?
back: By smoothly weighting asset allocations across regimes as probabilities evolve, avoiding the 100% turnover churn of hard binary switching when macro indicators hover near zero.

front: Common Misconception: Can smoothed Markov-switching probabilities be used to evaluate historical backtest performance?
back: No. Smoothed probabilities condition on future sample information unknown at trade dates, creating severe look-ahead bias that cannot be replicated in live trading.
